title: Retire current-view material only after resolving surviving dependencies
statement: The system shall permit compaction of superseded operational detail after resolving current reliance, while preserving unresolved obligations, meaningful completed accounts and explicitly retained engineering material under its applicable retention policy.

what.problem: Cleanup can discard uncommitted knowledge, active findings, current evidence, or links still needed by current engineering work.
what.desired_outcome: Maintainers can reduce obsolete working-view material while preserving current reliance and recoverable original history.

why.rationale: IR-003 requires retention of active work and current-reliance material and permits cleanup only after historical recoverability and dependency reconciliation.

stakeholders: Owners of surviving obligations and consumers

conditions: Before material leaves the current working view or the project releases retained material under a controlled retention-policy decision.

contexts: Candidate retired material, retained historical states, and surviving governed dependencies.

how.approach: Separate replaceable operational detail from explicitly retained engineering history. Resolve current obligations and reliance before compaction; no historical copy is required for superseded working information with no decision value. Retained Baselines, selected completion meaning and migration originals keep their applicable preservation rules.

how_much.scope: Governed engineering material and its declared current consumers. Removal from the current working view differs from destruction of retained history. No permanent duplicate archive, automatic age-based expiry, or universal retention duration is required. SR-007 governs authorization for destructive actions and policy changes. The local operational-history extension adds the criteria attributed to SRC-LOCAL-OPERATIONAL-ANALYSIS; retained product contracts and old allocation evidence do not establish implementation or coverage of that extension.

acceptance_criteria: For engineering definitions, retained Baselines and explicitly preserved history, cleanup identifies recoverable originals and reconciles consumers. Superseded working summaries and routine logs need no historical copy when no open obligation, current conclusion or explicit retention decision relies on them.

When active work, unresolved findings, required evidence, or another current dependency still relies on the material without a coherent replacement, removal is prevented and the unmet reliance is identified.
Uncommitted or otherwise unretained content cannot be described as historically recoverable without first establishing a retained recovery basis.

After permitted cleanup, current obligations and references remain usable without retrieving retired definitions to operate the current model, while historical inspection preserves the retired material's original meaning.

Age alone cannot decide usefulness. Operational detail may be discarded when current dependencies are resolved; release of explicitly retained engineering history remains subject to its selected retention policy.

Before retiring operational source files, current consumers and required evidence must have a coherent replacement or explicit disposition, and original content required for historical reliance remains recoverable. A successful import alone does not authorize deletion.
Replacing comparable working evidence cannot erase a failure for another scope. Unavailable discarded detail is reported honestly and cannot silently resolve to newer bytes.
